acme_integration_engineer: Hey, running into a production issue. We're using json_mode with nested items and keep getting JSON parse errors intermittently when streaming responses. Happening ~5% of requests.

mia_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact API request and a full raw response payload you received (including streaming chunk boundaries)? Also which model and whether streaming is true?

acme_integration_engineer: model=rwd-std-1, streaming=true. Here's the raw stream capture (copied from our proxy logs):

acme_integration_engineer: ```
data: {"items":[{"id":"i1","price":100,"meta":{"color":"red"}} 

data: {"items":[{"id":"i2","meta":{"color":"blue"},"extra":"x"}} 

data: {"items":[{"id":"i3","price":200}} 

acme_integration_engineer: Parser throws: JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 2 column 1 (char 57). Our client expects a single top-level object with "items" array.

jules_ml: thanks — looks like stream chunks are sending partial objects and, weirdly, duplicating the "items" key across chunks instead of streaming inside the same array. That would break most strict JSON parsers.

mia_support: can you confirm you're not concatenating multiple API responses? Also the repeated "items" key in separate chunks suggests the server is streaming repeated top-level fragments instead of streaming array elements.

acme_integration_engineer: we're definitely opening one request per call. We capture raw bytes; it shows three separate data chunks each starting with a new top-level object (see paste). Our client tries to reassemble by concatenation, which fails.

devon_runtime: looping in runtime. This looks like a structured-output + streaming interaction where the runtime tried to flush intermediate array entries as separate JSON documents. We have two failure modes: (1) streaming of independent top-level objects (which is NDJSON) and (2) streaming of partial tokens that cut an object in half. Both will break a strict JSON deserializer expecting one object.

devon_runtime: can you share the exact request body (prompts and any flags), especially the structured output settings (json_mode, array_mode, item_delimiter)? If you can't paste secrets, redact tokens/keys.

acme_integration_engineer: request body (redacted):
```
{
  "model":"rwd-std-1",
  "json_mode":"strict",
  "structured_output": {"root":"items","item_wrapper":"object","array_mode":"stream_chunks"},
  "stream": true,
  "prompt": "produce items array..."
}
```

mia_support: aha — array_mode:"stream_chunks" + json_mode:"strict" is a mismatch. strict expects a single valid JSON document. stream_chunks emits multiple top-level fragments. Two options: switch to json_mode:"ndjson" or set array_mode:"join_chunks" so the runtime will assemble a single array before finishing the response.

acme_integration_engineer: switching to ndjson isn't an option for us (we need a single array). We tried join_chunks but saw latency spikes >200ms as the runtime buffers. That caused customer complaints. Any way to keep streaming low-latency and still produce a single valid array?

devon_runtime: short-term: enable array_mode:"join_chunks" and reduce the buffer window to 50ms (trade slightly higher CPU for lower latency). Long-term: we'll implement a streaming-safe array mode that emits proper NDJSON element-per-line with an explicit wrapper header so clients can reconstruct without strict parsing failure.

sre_oncall_bot: FYI — observed traffic pattern match on the cluster. We saw backpressure and occasional retry loops from the client library (caused by parse failures) which increased request counts by ~1.6x for that customer during the spike window.

billing_bot: Noted potential billing impact — retries counted as additional usage. If this was an emergent platform behavior, we can create a bill adjustment ticket after root cause.

jules_ml: another subtle cause: some model outputs include extra keys in nested objects (e.g., "extra":"x" above) which can break clients that strictly validate schemas. For schema-stable consumers, recommend using a validation+filter step on the server side or the platform option "schema_strict":false which will filter unknown fields.

acme_integration_engineer: that extra key is problematic: our downstream pipelines rely on exact keys (id, price, meta). Any way to instruct the model/runtime to only emit those keys?

jules_ml: yes — include a schema prompt + enforcement flag: "output_schema": {"items": [{"id":"string","price":"number","meta":"object"}]}, and set "enforce_output_schema": true. Runtime will drop extra keys and can also return a warnings list.

mia_support: action items: (1) devon to add a short-term tweak to array_mode join buffering with configurable window and ship a canary; (2) jules to document schema enforcement flags in support KB; (3) billing to review potential overcharges for acme during the incident window.

devon_runtime: I'll open a runtime PR to add "array_mode_buffer_ms" (default 200 -> reduceable to 50) and a validation so json_mode:"strict" + array_mode:"stream_chunks" will return 400 with guidance instead of producing NDJSON. Will canary on 2 servers next week.

acme_integration_engineer: thanks — repro steps we used (to help):
1) curl -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @req.json
2) stream capture shows multiple top-level objects starting with "{\"items\":..." instead of single array
3) client concatenation -> JSONDecodeError

mia_support: thanks, that repro was super helpful. We'll follow up after the canary. If you'd like immediate mitigation, switch to array_mode:"join_chunks" and set array_mode_buffer_ms:50 and keep stream=true. Expect slightly higher p95 latency but preserved correctness.

billing_bot: I've created ticket BILL-7832 to track any adjustments — please paste request IDs if you want line-level exceptions.

acme_integration_engineer: pasted request ids in the ticket. appreciate the quick triage. :slightly_smiling_face:

mia_support: leaving this open until devon confirms canary and docs updated. Thanks everyone!
